Status: The MediaWiki API is a mature and stable interface that is actively supported and improved. While we try to avoid it, we may occasionally need to make breaking changes; subscribe to the mediawiki-api-announce mailing list for notice of updates.

Erroneous requests: When erroneous requests are sent to the API, an HTTP header will be sent with the key "MediaWiki-API-Error" and then both the value of the header and the error code sent back will be set to the same value. For more information see API: Errors and warnings.

Testing: For ease of testing API requests, see Special:ApiSandbox.

params.maxlag:
Maximum lag can be used when MediaWiki is installed on a database replicated cluster. To save actions causing any more site replication lag, this parameter can make the client wait until the replication lag is less than the specified value. In case of excessive lag, error code `maxlag` is returned with a message like `Waiting for $host: $lag seconds lagged`.
See Manual: Maxlag parameter for more information.
params.smaxage: Set the `s-maxage` HTTP cache control header to this many seconds. Errors are never cached.
params.maxage: Set the `max-age` HTTP cache control header to this many seconds. Errors are never cached.
params.assert: Verify that the user is logged in if set to `user`, not logged in if set to `anon`, or has the bot user right if `bot`.
params.assertuser: Verify the current user is the named user.
params.requestid: Any value given here will be included in the response. May be used to distinguish requests.
params.servedby: Include the hostname that served the request in the results.
params.curtimestamp: Include the current timestamp in the result.
params.responselanginfo: Include the languages used for uselang and errorlang in the result.
params.origin:
When accessing the API using a cross-domain AJAX request (CORS), set this to the originating domain. This must be included in any pre-flight request, and therefore must be part of the request URI (not the POST body).

For authenticated requests, this must match one of the origins in the `Origin` header exactly, so it has to be set to something like `https://en.wikipedia.org` or `https://meta.wikimedia.org`. If this parameter does not match the `Origin` header, a 403 response will be returned. If this parameter matches the `Origin` header and the origin is allowed, the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` headers will be set.

For non-authenticated requests, specify the value `*`. This will cause the `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header to be set, but `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials` will be `false` and all user-specific data will be restricted.
params.uselang: Language to use for message translations. `action=query&meta=siteinfo&siprop=languages` returns a list of language codes, or specify `user` to use the current user's language preference, or specify `content` to use this wiki's content language.
params.variant: Variant of the language. Only works if the base language supports variant conversion.
params.errorformat: Format to use for warning and error text output
params.errorlang: Language to use for warnings and errors. `action=query&meta=siteinfo&siprop=languages` returns a list of language codes, or specify `content` to use this wiki's content language, or specify `uselang` to use the same value as the uselang parameter.
params.errorsuselocal: If given, error texts will use locally-customized messages from the MediaWiki namespace.

params.callback: If specified, wraps the output into a given function call. For safety, all user-specific data will be restricted.
params.utf8: If specified, encodes most (but not all) non-ASCII characters as UTF-8 instead of replacing them with hexadecimal escape sequences. Default when formatversion is not `1`.
params.ascii: If specified, encodes all non-ASCII using hexadecimal escape sequences. Default when formatversion is `1`.

query.description:
Fetch data from and about MediaWiki.

All data modifications will first have to use query to acquire a token to prevent abuse from malicious sites.

params.export: Export the current revisions of all given or generated pages.
params.exportnowrap: Return the export XML without wrapping it in an XML result (same format as Special:Export). Can only be used with query+export.
params.exportschema: Target the given version of the XML dump format when exporting. Can only be used with query+export.
params.iwurl: Whether to get the full URL if the title is an interwiki link.
params.continue: When more results are available, use this to continue. More detailed information on how to continue queries can be found on mediawiki.org.
params.titles: A list of titles to work on.
params.pageids: A list of page IDs to work on.
params.revids: A list of revision IDs to work on. Note that almost all query modules will convert revision IDs to the corresponding page ID and work on the latest revision instead. Only `prop=revisions` uses exact revisions for its response.
params.generator:
Get the list of pages to work on by executing the specified query module.

Note: Generator parameter names must be prefixed with a "g", see examples.
params.redirects: Automatically resolve redirects in query+titles, query+pageids, and query+revids, and in pages returned by query+generator.
params.converttitles: Convert titles to other variants if necessary. Only works if the wiki's content language supports variant conversion. Languages that support variant conversion include ban, en, crh, gan, iu, kk, ku, shi, sr, tg, uz and zh.

params.expiry: Expiry time. May be relative (e.g. `5 months` or `2 weeks`) or absolute (e.g. `2014-09-18T12:34:56Z`). If set to `infinite`, `indefinite`, or `never`, the block will never expire.
params.anononly: Block anonymous users only (i.e. disable anonymous edits for this IP address).
params.autoblock: Automatically block the last used IP address, and any subsequent IP addresses they try to login from.
params.noemail: Prevent user from sending email through the wiki. (Requires the `blockemail` right).
params.hidename: Hide the username from the block log. (Requires the `hideuser` right).
params.allowusertalk: Allow the user to edit their own talk page (depends on $wgBlockAllowsUTEdit).
params.reblock: If the user is already blocked, overwrite the existing block.
params.watchuser: Watch the user's or IP address's user and talk pages.
params.tags: Change tags to apply to the entry in the block log.
params.partial: Block user from specific pages or namespaces rather than the entire site.
params.pagerestrictions: List of titles to block the user from editing. Only applies when partial is set to true.
params.namespacerestrictions: List of namespace IDs to block the user from editing. Only applies when partial is set to true.

clientlogin.description:
Log in to the wiki using the interactive flow.

The general procedure to use this module is:

Fetch the fields available from `action=query&meta=authmanagerinfo` with `amirequestsfor=login`, and a `login` token from `action=query&meta=tokens`.
Present the fields to the user, and obtain their submission.
Post to this module, supplying loginreturnurl and any relevant fields.
Check the `status` in the response.
If you received `PASS` or `FAIL`, you're done. The operation either succeeded or it didn't.
If you received `UI`, present the new fields to the user and obtain their submission. Then post to this module with logincontinue and the relevant fields set, and repeat step 4.
If you received `REDIRECT`, direct the user to the `redirecttarget` and wait for the return to loginreturnurl. Then post to this module with logincontinue and any fields passed to the return URL, and repeat step 4.
If you received `RESTART`, that means the authentication worked but we don't have a linked user account. You might treat this as `UI` or as `FAIL`.

params.loginrequests: Only use these authentication requests, by the `id` returned from `action=query&meta=authmanagerinfo` with `amirequestsfor=login` or from a previous response from this module.
params.loginmessageformat: Format to use for returning messages.
params.loginmergerequestfields: Merge field information for all authentication requests into one array.
params.loginpreservestate: Preserve state from a previous failed login attempt, if possible.
params.loginreturnurl:
Return URL for third-party authentication flows, must be absolute. Either this or logincontinue is required.

Upon receiving a `REDIRECT` response, you will typically open a browser or web view to the specified `redirecttarget` URL for a third-party authentication flow. When that completes, the third party will send the browser or web view to this URL. You should extract any query or POST parameters from the URL and pass them as a logincontinue request to this API module.
params.logincontinue: This request is a continuation after an earlier `UI` or `REDIRECT` response. Either this or loginreturnurl is required.

compare.description:
Get the difference between two pages.

A revision number, a page title, a page ID, text, or a relative reference for both "from" and "to" must be passed.

params.fromslots:
Override content of the revision specified by fromtitle, fromid or fromrev.

This parameter specifies the slots that are to be modified. Use fromtext-{slot}, fromcontentmodel-{slot}, and fromcontentformat-{slot} to specify content for each slot.
params.fromtext-{slot}: Text of the specified slot. If omitted, the slot is removed from the revision.
params.fromsection-{slot}: When fromtext-{slot} is the content of a single section, this is the section identifier. It will be merged into the revision specified by fromtitle, fromid or fromrev as if for a section edit.
params.fromcontentmodel-{slot}: Content model of fromtext-{slot}. If not supplied, it will be guessed based on the other parameters.
params.frompst: Do a pre-save transform on fromtext-{slot}.
params.torelative: Use a revision relative to the revision determined from fromtitle, fromid or fromrev. All of the other 'to' options will be ignored.
params.toslots:
Override content of the revision specified by totitle, toid or torev.

This parameter specifies the slots that are to be modified. Use totext-{slot}, tocontentmodel-{slot}, and tocontentformat-{slot} to specify content for each slot.
params.totext-{slot}: Text of the specified slot. If omitted, the slot is removed from the revision.
params.tosection-{slot}: When totext-{slot} is the content of a single section, this is the section identifier. It will be merged into the revision specified by totitle, toid or torev as if for a section edit.
params.tocontentmodel-{slot}: Content model of totext-{slot}. If not supplied, it will be guessed based on the other parameters.
params.topst: Do a pre-save transform on totext.
params.prop: Which pieces of information to get.
params.slots: Return individual diffs for these slots, rather than one combined diff for all slots.

params.undoafter: Undo all revisions from undo to this one. If not set, just undo one revision.

options.description:
Change preferences of the current user.

Only options which are registered in core or in one of installed extensions, or options with keys prefixed with `userjs-` (intended to be used by user scripts), can be set.

params.reset: Resets preferences to the site defaults.
params.resetkinds: List of types of options to reset when the reset option is set.
params.change: List of changes, formatted name=value (e.g. skin=vector). If no value is given (not even an equals sign), e.g., optionname|otheroption|..., the option will be reset to its default value. If any value passed contains the pipe character (`|`), use the alternative multiple-value separator for correct operation.
params.optionname: The name of the option that should be set to the value given by optionvalue.
params.optionvalue: The value for the option specified by optionname.

params.modules: List of module names (values of the action and format parameters, or `main`). Can specify submodules with a `+`, or all submodules with `+*`, or all submodules recursively with `+**`.

parse.description:
Parses content and returns parser output.

See the various prop-modules of `action=query` to get information from the current version of a page.

There are several ways to specify the text to parse:

Specify a page or revision, using page, pageid, or oldid.
Specify content explicitly, using text, title, revid, and contentmodel.
Specify only a summary to parse. prop should be given an empty value.

params.title: Title of page the text belongs to. If omitted, contentmodel must be specified, and API will be used as the title.
params.text: Text to parse. Use title or contentmodel to control the content model.
params.revid: Revision ID, for `{{REVISIONID}}` and similar variables.
params.page: Parse the content of this page. Cannot be used together with text and title.
params.pageid: Parse the content of this page. Overrides page.
params.redirects: If page or pageid is set to a redirect, resolve it.
params.oldid: Parse the content of this revision. Overrides page and pageid.
params.prop: Which pieces of information to get
params.wrapoutputclass: CSS class to use to wrap the parser output.
params.pst: Do a pre-save transform on the input before parsing it. Only valid when used with text.
params.onlypst: Do a pre-save transform (PST) on the input, but don't parse it. Returns the same wikitext, after a PST has been applied. Only valid when used with text.
params.section:
Only parse the content of the section with this identifier.

When `new`, parse text and sectiontitle as if adding a new section to the page.

`new` is allowed only when specifying text.
params.sectiontitle:
New section title when section is `new`.

Unlike page editing, this does not fall back to summary when omitted or empty.
params.disablelimitreport: Omit the limit report ("NewPP limit report") from the parser output.
params.disableeditsection: Omit edit section links from the parser output.
params.disablestylededuplication: Do not deduplicate inline stylesheets in the parser output.
params.showstrategykeys: Whether to include internal merge strategy information in jsconfigvars.
params.sectionpreview: Parse in section preview mode (enables preview mode too).
params.disabletoc: Omit table of contents in output.
params.useskin: Apply the selected skin to the parser output. May affect the following properties: `text`, `langlinks`, `headitems`, `modules`, `jsconfigvars`, `indicators`.
params.contentformat: Content serialization format used for the input text. Only valid when used with text.
params.contentmodel: Content model of the input text. If omitted, title must be specified, and default will be the model of the specified title. Only valid when used with text.

rollback.description:

query+prefixsearch.description:
Perform a prefix search for page titles.

Despite the similarity in names, this module is not intended to be equivalent to Special:PrefixIndex; for that, see `action=query&list=allpages` with the `apprefix` parameter. The purpose of this module is similar to `action=opensearch`: to take user input and provide the best-matching titles. Depending on the search engine backend, this might include typo correction, redirect avoidance, or other heuristics.

query+deletedrevs.description:
List deleted revisions.

Operates in three modes:

List deleted revisions for the given titles, sorted by timestamp.
List deleted contributions for the given user, sorted by timestamp (no titles specified).
List all deleted revisions in the given namespace, sorted by title and timestamp (no titles specified, druser not set).
Certain parameters only apply to some modes and are ignored in others.

params.drstart: The timestamp to start enumerating from.
params.drend: The timestamp to stop enumerating at.
params.drprefix: Search for all page titles that begin with this value.
params.drunique: List only one revision for each page.
params.drnamespace: Only list pages in this namespace.
params.drtag: Only list revisions tagged with this tag.
params.druser: Only list revisions by this user.
params.drexcludeuser: Don't list revisions by this user.
params.drlimit: The maximum amount of revisions to list.
params.drcontinue: When more results are available, use this to continue. More detailed information on how to continue queries can be found on mediawiki.org.

Also include local messages, i.e. messages that don't exist in the software but do exist as in the MediaWiki namespace.
This lists all MediaWiki-namespace pages, so it will also list those that aren't really messages such as Common.js.
